knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Open cuts are covered with a waterproof dressing before gloves go on, so the wound is not exposed to the spill.
Absorbent materials, PPE and contaminated cloths are sealed into a clinical waste bag. The sharps container is for sharps only, and general waste or drains are not permitted.
Sharps must never go into general waste and must be placed in an appropriate container, removed with a litter picker or grips.

practicalCriteria: Learner checks their own hands and covers a supplied mock cut with a waterproof dressing before putting on gloves, observed by the assessor.
Learner removes a mock sharp from a supplied practice spill using a litter picker or grips and places it into a rigid container, without touching it by hand.
Learner absorbs, disinfects and wipes a practice spill from the outside toward the centre, and states the disinfectant contact time from the supplied label.
Learner seals the clinical waste bag, disinfects a supplied reusable tool, and records the job, including the sharps count and materials used.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Assessor observation of the supervised practice spill, from protection through disposal
Photograph of the sealed clinical waste bag and the closed sharps container
Written confirmation that the learner has completed the employer's required training before any live task
stopWorkCriteria: Spill is large, the material is unidentified, or the worker cannot carry out the steps safely
Worker has an open cut without a dressing, or a needle stick or splash has occurred
Sharp is handled by hand or placed in general waste
Worker has not completed the employer's required training for this task
